The pre-merge unwired baseline file is retained unchanged as history.
stance: HONEST WIRED BASELINE — the corpus genuinely scores the Rust core, and the core is still the deliberately skeletal US-009 contract: only EOF (quirk Q20), state gating (quirk Q26), the action prelude, empty-chunk recording, and input/buffer/action limit behavior exist; every send path that passes the gates refuses with the non-oracle Unimplemented code, surfaced as the truthful CORE_BEHAVIOR_UNIMPLEMENTED envelope. 7 of 74 public scenarios pass because they exercise exactly that encoded slice — the core was NOT tuned toward any scenario, and the re-run after the re-review fix reproduced the identical pass set. The remaining 67 failures are the protocol-stub gate doing its job; closing them belongs to US-010..US-016. No story acceptance beyond US-009 is claimed.

review_round_1_fix.finding: us005.pub.0068 (send_text in closing) previously passed with the ADAPTER synthesizing the StateViolation (pre-delivery require_open) and the pending-action count; the core's equivalent gate never executed, contradicting the seven-genuine-passes attribution.
review_round_1_fix.fix: For every constructible command the driver now parses all fields in Java's exact read order and delivers the command; the core runs Java's interleaved gates itself (actionCount++/max_actions prelude, requireOpen, payload limit — the identical sequence in connection.rs handle_command). The begin_action/require_open driver-gate mirrors remain ONLY for steps that can never become a core input (missing/mistyped fields, unknown fields/actions, a send_close code outside the core's u16 command vocabulary), where Java's requireOpen-before-field-read ordering must still be shaped by the driver — input-shaping of malformed steps, verified line-by-line against the quarantined OracleEngine (Execution.action:412-430, sendText:432-439, sendFragment:477-496, requireOpen:546-550), not protocol behavior.
